facts.fact: Heroine is Neela, 27, odiyan of the Resin House, ledger number Seventeen. She does not know her birth name.
Love interest is Devan, 32, warden of Kettamala hill fort and the queen's border commander for the Monkey Pass.
Neela's night-shape is a leopard. Ammu's is a jackal, Vellan's a sloth bear, Kirri's a civet. Shapes are fixed at the first turning and never chosen.
An odiyan turns only after sunset, by smearing nightbark resin on throat and wrists. She turns back at first light and cannot turn back early, turn by day, or speak while in shape.
A witness is anyone who has seen a turning (dusk or dawn) with their own eyes. Seeing only the animal does not make someone a witness.
A witness who speaks the night-shape aloud in the odiyan's hearing, while she is in shape and before dawn, cages her for life. Intent does not matter. Non-witnesses cannot cage.
Caged odiyans stay animals for life and their human minds fade over about a year. No caging is ever undone.

Self-naming: during a dusk turning, an odiyan speaks her own night-shape to one chosen person looking at her. It voids all other witnesses, a caging then needs both their voices, her ledger witness entry burns, and she is marked rogue. It can be done only once in a life.
A self-named pair feel each other's wounds for life. A cut opens as a welt on the other, and a mortal wound drags the other toward death.
A ledger page in a true witness's resin-ink gives its holder a witness's power when read aloud at night in the odiyan's hearing. Pages cannot be forged.
Handing a page to its own subject requires the holder to read it aloud in full by daylight before her. A page held by its own subject cannot be used against her.
Each ledger page has the odiyan's intake roll (birth name, birth village) fastened to it. Self-naming burns only the witness entry. Burning the whole page destroys the intake roll.
Going a full moon without resin brings the ache: fever, night-sweats and split nails. Never fatal. Resin can be forced on an unwilling odiyan, which tears the resin scars.
Every odiyan has pale ridged resin scars at the throat and inner wrists.
Marma and kalari are skill, not magic. A marma strike can kill in human form.
Kettamala is a laterite hill fort above the Monkey Pass. Its west stair has a parrot newel post with a broken beak. The cistern chain clanks on the hour.
The warden's chamber has west-facing teak shutters, and the third slat creaks. The fort kalari is a sunken earthen pit below the east wall.
The Resin House is in the Blackbark Wood, a day's hard ride from Kettamala, and has kennels for caged odiyans.
Kodiyur is the royal port capital of Varanad. The palace sits on a sea cliff and the harbour tower fires a noon gun.
The monsoon closes the Monkey Pass and the hill roads for about four months.
Neela was married to Devan as the ward of the Chirayil pepper house, at a match pressed by the queen's council and proposed by Councillor Ittan.
Ammu, 25, is Neela's guild-sister, raised beside her since age 5, and calls her chechi. Ammu witnessed Neela's first turning.
Asha, Devan's younger sister and second at the fort, was killed at 22 on the west stair six years before book 1.
Janu, 61, steward of Kettamala, raised Devan and Asha after their mother died.
Captain Muthu, 35, is Devan's second-in-command and secretly writes monthly reports to the queen's household.
Ruler is Queen Nirmala of Varanad, 54. The guild master is Chathu, 61, not an odiyan. Councillor Ittan, 49, is Keeper of the Passes.
Neela wears a plain gold wedding bangle from the wedding onward.
Forged pass-tokens reaching Thurai raiders bear genuine council wax. The queen seals in green wax.
Kirri wears a silver anklet, which she still wears when caged in the kennels.
Neela's contract is her twelfth. Twelve completed contracts are promised to earn release.
Book 1 opens on the wedding day, about 40 days before the monsoon closes the pass, which is Neela's contract deadline.
Devan has not sparred a living person in eight years. He drills kalari alone every dawn.
Border wardens are taught the odiyan witness rule. Devan knows it from the start.
The coastal raiders come from Thurai, a rival kingdom ruled by sea lords.
The Resin House owns the only nightbark groves and rations resin. Rogues must steal resin or buy it cut with lamp oil.
Kannan is a goat-boy of about nine or ten; Chinna runs the kitchen door; Raiu is a young guard who holds the corridor torch outside the warden's chamber.
Devan tells Neela the night guard layout: two on the west stair, four at the padippura, six on the wall in pairs, changing on the third clank after the middle watch.
Devan lays his sword on the floor on Neela's side of the bed, hilt toward her; the grip is plain wire, worn at the thumb.
Neela carries the guild's leopard tooth sewn into her waistband and the resin in a corked flask in a fold of her cloth.
Devan says he took four months and asked twice to learn Raiu's name.
Devan first smelled nightbark resin at twenty, from a sealed jar passed around a classroom during his border training on the witness rule.
Janu says it is the first time in eleven years Devan has asked for food himself.
Gopan is the old keeper of the cistern chain and wheel, nineteen years in the post, who missed one hour in 'the fever year'.
Bhaskaran is the sergeant at the padippura. Unni is a thin young guard whose mother sells salt fish in the lower village.
The day watch changes on the sixth clank of the cistern chain after dawn.
Pepper is Kannan's white goat, who bites.
Janu says Devan used to have a kalari partner and now trains alone, a gap of eight years.
The hounds of Kettamala number fourteen and sleep in a long kennel behind the stables; before the wedding they ran the yard loose from dusk to dawn.

Bhaskaran passed a salt-and-cloth cart from the coast through his gate at the last new moon on the strength of a council-wax tally, and the tally number matches the one found in the dead raider's satchel.
Genuine council wax is dull brick red, pressed with a pepper-sprig mark, and poured with clove oil so it does not crack in damp. The forged tally's wax is about a month old.
Devan tells Neela the pass-seller is someone on the queen's council and that he does not know who; he says the raiders' next targets are the coast-side villages.
Neela finds a gap of about thirty counts under the far wall when the lower wall pair swings inward, and one sentry paces the walk above the warden's window.
Bhaskaran led the patrol to the second ford at dawn after a herdsman reported men there.

Neela notices that Devan's only untrue statement is 'Rain' at dusk under a clear sky; it is the single thing he will not say plainly. She links it to the kennelled hounds as both being about the dark.

Neela notices that 'Rain' at dusk under a clear sky is the one answer Devan gives that is not an answer; it sounds like a forecast but fits nothing in the sky. She links it and the kennelled hounds as both being about the dark. She does not conclude he lies.
Kannan's loft sits over the kennel wall; the hounds howl until the middle watch.
Chinna sleeps on a mat at the kitchen door; the granary has a farm lock.
Janu says Devan has slept badly for eight years.
On the night of chapter 4 Neela counts thirty-seven nights left before the pass closes.
Captain Muthu was Devan's kalari partner before Devan stopped sparring eight years ago, and he asks for a round every seventh day.
Kannan's mother is named Bindu and sings; Neela learned this from women at the well.
Neela's cover guardian is Kunjan Chirayil, who kept the Chirayil north warehouse in Kodiyur.
Asha came to the fort at nineteen and in her first month wrote every recruit's name and mother's village on a slate.

The sentry Devan has pulled off the rampart is the one above the warden's window (ch 4 placement), not below it as the outline says; Devan lifts the shutter bar and leaves it against the wall that night.

Devan has the sentry above the warden's window (ch 4 placement, not below as the outline says) pulled, but leaves the shutter bar in its usual place across the shutters; Neela must lift it herself as on previous nights.
Janu found Asha's body on the west stair the morning after she was killed.
Devan spent two years at a border school, where he learned the witness rule and first smelled nightbark resin.
Devan's father is dead; Devan respected him, and fondness came after his death.
Neela wears a day kasavu from her trousseau on the terraces and tears its gold border to bind Kannan's hand.

knowledge.knows: Her contract terms: kill Devan in his chamber so it looks like a leopard kill, before the pass closes.
Her only witnesses are Chathu and Ammu, and her page is in the ledger.
She was lookout on a hill-fort job six years ago where a young woman died. She was moved there blindfolded and does not know which fort.
She does not know the buyer of her contract, her birth name, or the self-naming loophole.
The witness rule, and that Asha's bear wounds inside the walls mean an odiyan contract killed her.
Forged pass-tokens with real council wax reach Thurai raiders. He does not know who sells them.
The council pressed the marriage, and he distrusts the bride.
The self-naming loophole, told to no one. She has had no answer to her letters to Kirri.
Every member's shape and page; that release is a lie; the buyer of Devan's contract and the queen's seal on it.
He killed Asha and Neela was lookout. He suspects release is a lie.
He bought Devan's contract, sells extra pass-tokens, and planned to take the pass-seal from Devan's widow.
Her secret treaty with Thurai, her seal on the contract writ, and the crown leaf of night-guard pages.
He reports on Devan to the queen's household. He knows nothing of the contract or the treaty.

timeline.event: Neela is born in a village on the coast side of the Monkey Pass.
Raiders burn Neela's village. At 6 she is sold to the Resin House.
Ammu, age 5, is brought to the Resin House.
Neela's first turning at 16, witnessed by Chathu and Ammu (14).
Devan, 24, kills a surrendering raider captain with a marma strike and stops sparring.
Asha, 22, is killed on Kettamala's west stair by Vellan. Neela, 21, keeps watch.
Devan, 27, is made warden of Kettamala.
Kirri is 'released' and secretly caged in the kennels.
Neela and Devan marry at sunset. That night Devan secretly witnesses her turning.
Monsoon closes the Monkey Pass. This is the contract deadline.
